<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments and a package() function definition in the global scope. There is no pkgver() function, no executable code in the top-level scope (such as command substitutions, curls, or evals), and no code that would run during the sourcing of the PKGBUILD for makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare or makepkg --printsrcinfo. The source URLs point to the official GitHub releases of the tldraw-offline project, and checksums are provided. The package() function, which contains the actual installation logic, is not executed during these commands due to the --nobuild and --noprepare flags. Therefore, fetching and sourcing this PKGBUILD poses no security risk in this narrow gate.
</details>

audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/tldraw-offline-bin.git...
Cloned tldraw-offline-bin
Analyzing tldraw-offline-bin AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD only defines variables and a `source` array that points to the project's own GitHub release URLs (a .deb and an AppImage). The `--noprepare` flag prevents any `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions from running, so no maintainer scripts or extraction commands are executed during the source fetch and PKGBUILD sourcing. The URLs are the upstream project's official releases, and checksums are provided for the binary artifacts. No network requests to untrusted hosts, no code download/execution beyond standard extraction, and no use of dangerous constructs like `eval`, `curl|bash`, or obfuscated payloads. Therefore, running the specified commands is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
PKGBUILD fetches upstream release files; no malicious execution occurs.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- PKGBUILD fetches upstream release files; no malicious execution occurs.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD downloads binaries exclusively from the project's official GitHub releases (github.com/tldraw/tldraw-offline) over HTTPS, pinned to tag v${pkgver} with valid SHA-256 checksums. Both architectures use upstream-native distribution formats (a .deb for x86_64 and an AppImage for aarch64) and are extracted with standard tools (bsdtar, AppImage --appimage-extract). All subsequent operations — file installation, desktop entry normalization via sed, symlink creation, and license copying — are confined to the package's own ${pkgdir} tree and reflect ordinary Arch packaging workflow. No obfuscation, no execution of fetched code, no writes outside the application scope, and no network activity beyond the declared upstream source are present.
</details>
<evidence>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file is a standard package metadata file for an AUR binary package. It declares two prebuilt binary sources (a .deb for x86_64 and an .AppImage for aarch64) fetched from the project's own GitHub release server (github.com/tldraw/tldraw-offline/releases/download/v1.15.0/). Both sources are pinned to a specific release tag and have valid, non-SKIP sha256 checksums, which is proper packaging hygiene. The dependencies, noextract directives, and build options (!strip, !debug) are all consistent with standard practices for shipping prebuilt binaries. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unexpected file operations, data exfiltration, or code execution from untrusted hosts.
</details>
<evidence>
